chapter_theme: Reviling release (முத்திநிந்தை): those who deny a higher state, ignore the guru's sign, or take their own mind for God wander outside, unable to see the way shown them, while the Lord stands within and the short way is mantra and the inner fire.
structure_note: Most verses describe the deniers and the deluded (2558 to 2560, 2562, 2565); between them, 2561 and 2563 set the Lord who stays and pervades against them, and 2564 names the way.

2558.reading: The world knows that those who say there is no higher state go the way of hell; going from door to door, they begin to taste an evil end.
2558.nuance: பரகதி (the higher state) is set against நரகதி (the way to hell). Line 1 can be read of those who say 'there is' and those who say 'there is not', that is of all who argue over it, or only of the deniers. இரகதி and துரகதி are obscure: இரகதி is taken here with இரத்தல் (begging), துரகதி as துர்கதி (an evil end).

2559.reading: Those who cannot join the mark the guru set, and do not seek it, wander about talking fine words; they cannot sing of what he gave, so what gain can they have beside those who know it and can dance?
2559.nuance: குறி (the mark, the sign) is what the guru points to, taken as the goal of practice. The last two lines are compressed: they may contrast the talkers with those who know the gift and dance, or ask what gain either has.

2560.reading: Something goes out and comes into my heart; taking the opened mind for God, I called it that other Lord beyond all, and 'I am free of death; what is this here?' he says.
2560.nuance: In this chapter the verse reads most naturally as the self-deluded seeker who mistakes his own mind (சிந்தை) for God and declares himself deathless, and the speaker's 'I' as dramatic. அறப்பட்ட may mean 'beyond dharma' or 'cut off'; the voice of the last line is unclear.

2561.reading: As water does not stay on raised ground and a ship does not stay at sea but comes to harbour, the mighty Lord, showing the real thing that does not stay in the body, stood there.
2561.nuance: Both images are of things that move on to where they belong. உறுபொருள் (the real thing) that does not stay in the body may be the soul or the truth, and அடலிடை வண்ணன் (the one of mighty form) is taken as Siva.

2562.reading: Their hindrance is as weak as lotus thread, yet it spreads; wanting a way out they wander outside, and the wretched, shown the way to see, cannot see, and so wander on the evil path.
2562.nuance: தாமரை நூல்போல் தடுப்பார் may mean those who would hold back the Supreme with a lotus fibre, a futile effort, or a bond as fine as lotus fibre that still holds them. கலதி (the wretched) and காணாக் (unseeing) are plain.

2563.reading: People who reach their end without concealment join Nandi by fixing on him; the others cannot conceive the form that runs through forest, hill, field and every place.
2563.nuance: மூடுதல் இன்றி (without covering) is taken as without the veil of ignorance; the contrast in the last two lines is supplied, since the verse does not name the second group.

2564.reading: While the gods go south and north, west and east, the short way is to hold the mantra on the tongue and burn the fire in the centre, and so you will shine.
2564.nuance: குறுவழி (the short way) is set against the gods' journeys in all directions. நடு அங்கி (the fire in the middle) is traditionally taken as the inner fire of yoga in the central channel; it may also be the fire of a rite.

2565.reading: Though they look on in bewilderment they do no great tapas, and they do not hold to the concentration taught for their good; the evildoers who speak to provoke anger stood bearing heavy karma for themselves.
2565.nuance: தாரணை (dharana, fixing the mind) is the sixth limb of yoga. The verse turns the scorners' words back on them: what they say in anger becomes their own load of deeds.

source_issues: 2560: line 2 reads சிந்தையைப் தெய்வம், a misprint for சிந்தையைத் தெய்வம்.
2563: line 4 reads உன்னிகிலாரே, probably for உன்னகிலாரே.
2558: இரகதி and துரகதி are obscure and may be corrupt.

links.note: 2558: those who say there is no higher state (பரகதி இல்லை) go the way of hell, as the world knows. Kural 850: one who says 'it is not' to what the world says is (உண்டென்பது இல்லென்பான்) is set down on earth as a demon. Both condemn the denier and both appeal to the world's agreement (ஞாலம் அறியும், உலகத்தார்); the Kural places the penalty in this life, Tirumular in the next.

2559 is a near-verbatim repeat of 2093: those who cannot reach the guru's mark (குரு வைத்த குறி) wander making fine talk, and cannot sing what he did; what gain have they? In 2093 it stands among laments over ruin, in 2559 among the scorners of release; the repetition marks the talker without the guru's mark as a fixed type in the book.

On the reading that 2560 mocks a seeker who takes his opened mind (திறப்பட்ட சிந்தை) for God and calls it the Lord beyond all, it conflicts with 1555, where the abiding one is மனோமயன், the one who dwells in the mind, and those who scorn this are fools. 1555 calls the mind the place to worship and reach him; 2560 treats equating mind and God as delusion. The tension depends on 2560's voice being satirical, which the chapter suggests but the verse does not state.

2562: the wretched (கலதிகள்), shown the way to see (காண்வழி காட்ட), cannot see (கண் காணா). Kural 849: one who shows the unseeing (காணாதான் காட்டுவான்) himself does not see, and the unseeing sees only as he already saw. Both use showing and not seeing for the fool beyond teaching; the Kural adds that the shower is the one shamed.

2563: the others cannot conceive the form that runs through (ஊடும்) forest, hill, field and every place. 2639: like jaggery in cane and fragrance in the flower, our Lord stands mingled everywhere (எங்குங் கலந்துநின்றானே). Both say the Lord pervades all; 2639 gives the images, 2563 says failing to see this is what keeps one from him.

2564: while the gods go south, north, west and east, the short way (குறுவழி) is the mantra on the tongue and the fire within. 509: there are holy waters inside the heart, and those who do not bathe there wander over hollow and height (பள்ளமும் மேடும் பரந்து திரிவரே). Both set an inward practice against roaming in space, whether gods to the quarters or pilgrims over the land.

2565: the evildoers who speak to provoke anger stand bearing heavy karma (வல்வினை) for themselves. 538: one who reviles the jnani (ஞானியை நிந்திப்பவன்) takes on his deeds, as the worshipper takes his good. Both say scorn of the holy returns as karma on the scorner; 538 adds that it is a transfer from the one scorned, on the usual reading of its compressed lines.
